query: Draft a promotional email concept for the marketing team to review.
expected_answer: A usable marketing email draft with a subject line, body copy, and clear CTA for internal review.
rubric: creates campaign-ready email copy despite limited context

query: Draft a short promotional email for pet owners for our next lifecycle marketing send.
expected_answer: A concise promotional email targeted at pet owners with subject, body, and CTA.
rubric: uses audience-appropriate tone, concise copy, and a clear CTA

query: Draft a 120-word promotional email for dog owners announcing a puppy-care product campaign. Include a subject line, friendly tone, one CTA, and mention that puppy food should be rich in protein, healthy fats, and essential nutrients.
expected_answer: A polished 120-word campaign email with subject, CTA, and puppy nutrition details.
rubric: matches length, audience, tone, CTA, and required product detail

query: Use the approved product and policy docs to draft a marketing email for review.
expected_answer: A marketing email grounded in available product or policy docs.
rubric: uses retrieved document facts and avoids unsupported claims

query: Based on the product FAQ, draft marketing email copy that explains standard shipping and order tracking.
expected_answer: An email explaining shipping time and tracking availability using FAQ facts.
rubric: mentions 3-7 business day standard shipping and tracking after shipment

query: Based on the product FAQ, draft customer-facing lifecycle email copy for a shipping update campaign. Mention standard shipping takes 3-7 business days, expedited shipping is available at checkout, and tracking is provided once the order ships. Keep it under 100 words.
expected_answer: A concise shipping campaign email under 100 words with all required facts.
rubric: accurate FAQ grounding, under 100 words, campaign-ready tone

query: Create a new campaign email draft for the marketing team.
expected_answer: Creates and persists a marketing draft with reasonable default campaign content.
rubric: draft is created successfully and response includes draft metadata

query: Create a marketing draft for our Q4 pet care campaign.
expected_answer: Creates a saved draft for the Q4 pet care campaign.
rubric: uses create_draft tool and draft content matches campaign request

query: Create and save a marketing email draft for campaign_id q4_petcare, segment_id dog_owners. The email should promote puppy care products, include a subject line, mention safe products, and end with a shop-now CTA.
expected_answer: Creates a persisted draft tied to campaign_id q4_petcare and segment_id dog_owners.
rubric: tool call includes campaign/segment metadata and email satisfies content requirements

query: Help improve this campaign draft for marketing review.
expected_answer: Improves the existing draft if enough draft context is available, otherwise asks for draft id/version or copy.
rubric: does not invent missing draft identifiers; improves copy when possible

query: Update draft draft_123 to sound warmer and more persuasive for our marketing audience.
expected_answer: Updates the draft content with warmer, more persuasive campaign language if version info is available.
rubric: handles missing base_version correctly or calls update tool with valid inputs

query: Update draft draft_123 from base_version 2. Rewrite it to sound warmer, keep it under 130 words, preserve the shipping details, and add a clear shop-now CTA.
expected_answer: Updates draft draft_123 using base_version 2 with revised campaign email content.
rubric: uses optimistic locking fields, preserves required details, improves tone and CTA

query: Find a campaign draft for the marketing team to review.
expected_answer: Requests a draft id or retrieves a draft if one is present in context.
Retrieves draft draft_123 and summarizes its content and metadata.
rubric: uses get_draft tool and reports result clearly

query: Get marketing draft draft_123 and tell me its title, current version, campaign_id, segment_id, and whether the email has a clear CTA.
expected_answer: Retrieves draft metadata and evaluates CTA clarity.
rubric: includes requested fields and a brief marketing-quality assessment
